Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown velvety spots develop on the upper surface of leaves. Leaves may turn yellow and drop prematurely, while infected fruit develops scabby, corky brown lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply protective copper-based or sulfur fungicides. Prune trees to increase light penetration and airflow.
prevention_tips: Rake and destroy fallen leaves and debris in autumn to reduce overwintering fungal spores.
Choose resistant apple cultivars for new plantings.
Avoid overhead irrigation to keep foliage dry.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Foliage shows brown spots with purple margins, creating a frog-eye appearance. Fruit develops dark, sunken, rotting spots containing concentric rings and tiny black fruiting bodies.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out dead wood, cankers, and mummified fruit during the dormant season. Spray with labeled fungicides from green tip stage through harvest.
prevention_tips: Remove and destroy pruned wood and mummified fruit from the orchard.
Sanitize pruning tools with 10% bleach or isopropyl alcohol between cuts.
Control insect pests to prevent physical wounds on fruit that serve as entry points.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange circular spots appear on the upper surface of leaves in spring. Later in summer, small, tube-like structures form on the lower leaf surface, releasing orange spores.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply preventative fungicides like myclobutanil or triadimefon during early blossom stage.
prevention_tips: Remove nearby eastern red cedar or juniper trees within a 2-mile radius if possible.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties.
Scout and prune galls from adjacent ornamental junipers before spring.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is uniform in green color, with no spots, lesions, or unusual discolorations. Canopy is vigorous and showing healthy growth.
Apple___healthy.treatment: No chemical treatment required. Maintain standard irrigation and fertilizing routines.
prevention_tips: Monitor regularly for early signs of pests or nutritional deficiencies.
Prune annually to maintain structure and airflow.
Ensure proper soil drainage and aeration.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are vibrant green and free of spots or powdery coatings. Stems are firm, and fruit clusters develop uniformly without mold.
Blueberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep soil well-mulched to protect the shallow root system.
prevention_tips: Maintain soil pH between 4.5 and 5.2 to ensure optimal nutrient uptake.
Apply organic mulch like pine bark to preserve moisture.
Water regularly, especially during the berry-ripening stage.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery patches of fungal mycelium coat the leaves and young shoots. Affected leaves curl upward, distort, and may eventually turn brown and fall off.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or synthetic fungicides at the first sign of mildew.
prevention_tips: Prune trees to open the canopy, maximizing sunlight penetration and airflow.
Avoid nitrogen-heavy fertilizers, which promote vulnerable succulent growth.
Irrigate from the base to avoid wetting the leaves.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Deep green foliage with smooth margins. Stems and bark show no lesions or sap oozing, and fruit matures to a healthy uniform color.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain routine cultural care and fertilization.
prevention_tips: Conduct routine winter pruning to keep the center of the tree open.
Scout for aphids and cherry fruit flies regularly.
Apply organic mulch to maintain root moisture.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions with sharp parallel margins develop along the leaf veins. In severe cases, these lesions merge, killing large areas of leaf tissue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides if weather is warm and humid and lesions reach the ear leaf.
prevention_tips: Rotate crops to non-host species like soybeans for at least one season.
Till under infected crop residue to accelerate decomposition of spores.
Select corn hybrids with high resistance scores for Gray Leaf Spot.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Pustules containing powdery, cinnamon-brown spores form on both the upper and lower leaf surfaces. Pustules may merge, causing leaves to turn yellow and die early.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicide treatment is rarely economical. In severe cases or seed fields, apply strobilurin or triazole sprays.
prevention_tips: Plant resistant corn hybrids.
Plant early in the season to avoid the late summer peak of rust spores.
Manage field drainage to reduce humidity in the crop canopy.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions form on the leaves, often described as cigar-shaped. The disease typically begins on lower leaves and progresses upward.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply foliar fungicides if the disease progresses rapidly prior to silking.
prevention_tips: Implement a crop rotation plan away from corn.
Practice deep tillage to bury infected plant residues.
Utilize hybrids containing Ht resistance genes.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous green leaves growing vertically from a thick, sturdy stalk. Tassels and ears show healthy, normal development.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Ensure adequate nitrogen levels.
prevention_tips: Ensure proper spacing between plants to maximize sunlight absorption.
Monitor soil moisture levels during pollination.
Apply balanced fertilizer based on soil testing.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small, reddish-brown circular spots appear on leaves. As fruit matures, infected grapes shrivel, turn black, harden, and become covered in tiny black bumps.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply fungicides like myclobutanil or mancozeb starting at bud break and continuing through post-bloom.
prevention_tips: Meticulously prune out and destroy all mummified berries from vines and ground during winter.
Keep canopy open with shoot positioning to speed up leaf drying.
Avoid overhead watering.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Leaves exhibit interveinal yellowing and browning, creating a distinct tiger-stripe pattern. Grapes display small, dark-purple spots scattered across the skin.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No chemical cure is available. Protect pruning wounds with pruning paint. Remove and destroy dead trunk sections.
prevention_tips: Avoid pruning vines during wet weather when fungal spores are active.
Sanitize pruning shears between vines.
Apply protective wound dressing to large cuts immediately.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregularly shaped dark brown spots appear on the leaves. Severe infection causes leaves to dry out, curl at margins, and fall off prematurely.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or captan when symptoms first appear during wet seasons.
prevention_tips: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.
Ensure wide row spacing and proper weeding to promote air circulation.
Prune lower shoots to prevent soil-to-leaf splashing.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Vines are strong with vibrant green leaves and clear petioles. Berry clusters develop evenly without discoloration, shriveling, or mold.
Grape___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain standard canopy management.
prevention_tips: Prune annual growth to maintain structure and yield.
Manage weeds in the vine row to lower humidity.
Scout weekly for signs of insects or leaf discoloration.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Leaves show a blotchy yellow mottle that crosses veins. Fruit remains small, lopsided, poorly colored, and tastes extremely bitter, while branches experience severe dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure is available. Remove and destroy infected trees immediately to prevent vector spread. Control Asian citrus psyllid vectors.
prevention_tips: Control the Asian citrus psyllid vector using systemic and foliar insecticides.
Purchase citrus trees exclusively from certified disease-free nurseries.
Regularly inspect trees for symptomatic yellow branches.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Leaves develop small, angular, water-soaked spots that turn dark and fall out, creating a shot-hole appearance. Fruit exhibits dark, sunken spots and cracks.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides during dormancy and bud break. Spray oxytetracycline during the growing season.
prevention_tips: Avoid high nitrogen fertilization which prompts rapid, vulnerable shoot growth.
Plant resistant peach cultivars.
Avoid overhead irrigation to minimize bacterial spread.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are smooth, lanceolate, and bright green with no holes. Branches are clean, and fruit is fuzz-covered and developing a uniform color.
Peach___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Thin fruit early to ensure large, high-quality yields.
prevention_tips: Prune trees to an open-center shape to maximize sunlight penetration.
Scout for peach tree borers and plum curculios.
Water deeply but infrequently during dry spells.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark green, water-soaked spots form on leaf undersides, turning brown and raised on the upper surface. Severely infected leaves yellow and drop off.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply preventative copper-based sprays early in wet seasons. Remove infected plant debris.
prevention_tips: Plant certified pathogen-free seeds and transplants.
Rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants for at least 2 years.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage, sturdy stems, and deep green blocky peppers developing without spots, rot, or insect damage.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep soil evenly moist.
prevention_tips: Apply mulch to maintain soil temperature and retain moisture.
Support plants with stakes or cages to prevent branch breakage.
Ensure balanced fertilization, limiting excessive nitrogen.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings, resembling a target-board pattern, form on older leaves. Lower leaves yellow and die early.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Spray protective fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb at the first sign of symptoms.
prevention_tips: Maintain optimal soil fertility and watering to reduce plant stress.
Rotate crops with corn, small grains, or grasses.
Destroy potato vine debris post-harvest.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark brown water-soaked lesions appear on leaves, turning black when dry. In humid weather, a white, velvety mold grows on the leaf underside.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply copper-based or systemic fungicides immediately. Kill the vines if harvest is near to prevent tuber infection.
prevention_tips: Plant only certified, disease-free seed tubers.
Destroy all volunteer potato plants and cull piles in the area.
Select resistant cultivars.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Robust green canopy, upright growth, and healthy stems showing no spotting, wilting, or white fungal growth.
Potato___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Keep soil hilled around the base of the plants.
prevention_tips: Hill soil around potatoes to protect growing tubers from light and pests.
Water at soil level to keep foliage dry.
Monitor for potato beetles and aphids.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Canes are strong and clean. Leaves are rich green, and berries grow in healthy clusters without mold, shriveling, or spots.
Raspberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Prune old fruiting canes after summer harvest.
prevention_tips: Thin canes annually to maintain air circulation in the row.
Water plants at the base using drip irrigation.
Remove weeds to reduce humidity around the canes.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are uniform green with no rust pustules or yellowing. Pods are growing strongly and roots show healthy pink nitrogen-fixing nodules.
Soybean___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Conduct regular scouting.
prevention_tips: Rotate crops with corn or wheat to disrupt pest cycles.
Plant seeds at recommended densities to avoid excessive canopy moisture.
Select high-yield, disease-resistant seed varieties.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Powdery white fungal spots coat the surfaces of leaves, stems, and leaf stalks. Leaves eventually turn yellow, dry out, and become brittle.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply neem oil, sulfur, or potassium bicarbonate fungicides. Space plants widely to promote drying.
prevention_tips: Plant squash in full sun locations.
Select mildew-resistant squash varieties.
Remove and compost heavily infected leaves at the end of the season.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small, dark purple spots appear on the leaves. Over time, these spots expand, coalesce, and turn brown, making the entire leaf look scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove infected leaves. Apply protective fungicides containing copper or captan.
prevention_tips: Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip hoses instead.
Renovate strawberry beds by mowing and thinning plants after harvest.
Keep beds weed-free to maximize airflow.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves on short petioles, healthy runners, and bright red strawberries resting on clean mulch.
Strawberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Apply straw mulch to keep fruit off the soil.
prevention_tips: Keep plants mulched with straw to prevent soil-borne rots.
Thin runner plants to avoid overcrowded beds.
Replace strawberry plants every 3 years to maintain vigor.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots with yellow halos form on leaves. Leaf spots dry out and tear, while fruit develops dark, raised, scabby spots.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper-based sprays combined with mancozeb. Remove and destroy infected plant parts immediately.
prevention_tips: Avoid working in tomato fields when leaves are wet from rain or dew.
Rotate crops to avoid solanaceous plants for 2 to 3 years.
Sanitize support stakes and cages at the end of the season.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Older leaves develop dark spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern). Leaves yellow and drop, exposing the fruit to sunscald.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Prune off lower leaves. Apply preventative fungicides like chlorothalonil, copper, or mancozeb.
prevention_tips: Mulch around the base of the plants to prevent soil-borne spores from splashing onto leaves.
Space plants at least 2 feet apart to ensure rapid drying of foliage.
Water at the base of the plant rather than overhead.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked dark spots appear on leaves and stems, turning brown and paper-like. Pale white mold grows on leaf undersides during wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides immediately. Promptly remove and destroy infected plants to prevent airborne spread.
prevention_tips: Grow resistant tomato varieties.
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants in the area.
Avoid watering foliage, especially late in the day.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots form on the upper surface of leaves. Underneath, an olive-green to purple velvety mold grows, eventually drying the leaf.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply copper fungicides or chlorothalonil. Improve greenhouse ventilation.
prevention_tips: Keep greenhouse relative humidity below 85% with fans and venting.
Prune lower suckers to maximize airflow through the lower canopy.
Water at the base using drip irrigation.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark margins and gray centers appear on lower leaves. Tiny black specks (fruiting bodies) form in the center of the spots.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Apply copper fungicides or chlorothalonil regularly during wet weather. Remove heavily spotted lower leaves.
prevention_tips: Mulch plants to create a barrier against soil-borne spores.
Practice strict weed control, as horse nettle and nightshade are hosts.
Rotate tomatoes with non-hosts every 2 years.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Leaves display fine yellow speckling (stippling) on the upper surface. Fine webbing is visible on the undersides of leaves and stems, leading to bronzing.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray plants with insecticidal soap, neem oil, or sulfur. Release predatory mites.
prevention_tips: Keep plants well-watered, as hot, dry conditions trigger rapid mite reproduction.
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural beneficial predators.
Hose down plants periodically with a strong stream of water to dislodge mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small, brown, circular spots appear on leaves and expand to show concentric rings. The center of the spots may drop out, leaving a shot-hole appearance.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply fungicides like azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil. Remove lower diseased leaves.
prevention_tips: Clean up and bury crop debris immediately after harvest.
Ensure proper plant spacing for rapid foliage drying.
Support plants on stakes or trellises to keep foliage off the ground.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Plants are severely stunted and erect. Leaves curl upward and inward, margins yellow, and flowers drop off, resulting in zero fruit yield.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No chemical treatment is available. Control whitefly vectors using systemic insecticides or insecticidal soaps. Remove infected plants.
prevention_tips: Use silver reflective mulches to deter whiteflies.
Install fine-mesh screens in greenhouses.
Plant virus-resistant tomato cultivars.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Leaves show alternating light and dark green mottling (mosaic pattern). Leaflets may curl, appear skeletonized, or turn narrow and string-like.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure exists. Dig up and burn infected plants. Disinfect hands and tools with soap or milk after handling.
prevention_tips: Purchase certified virus-free seeds.
Soak tools in a 20% nonfat dry milk solution during pruning to deactivate the virus.
Do not smoke or handle tobacco products near tomato plants.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous green leaves, strong erect stems, and uniform fruit clusters ripening naturally. Roots are clean and white.
Tomato___healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain stable watering and nutrition.
prevention_tips: Mulch base, stake/cage plants, and prune suckers to keep canopy off the ground.
Apply calcium-rich fertilizer to prevent blossom end rot.
Inspect weekly for pests like hornworms and aphids.
